legend: JATC loves Banh-mi (a Vietnamese food). His affection for Banh-mi is so much that he always has it for breakfast. This morning, as usual, he buys a Banh-mi and decides to enjoy it in a special way.

First, he splits the Banh-mi into n%%ZSMJ0%% parts, places them on a row and numbers them from 1%%ZSMJ1%% through n%%ZSMJ2%%. For each part i%%ZSMJ3%%, he defines the deliciousness of the part as xi∈{0,1}%%ZSMJ4%%. JATC's going to eat those parts one by one. At each step, he chooses arbitrary remaining part and eats it. Suppose that part is the i%%ZSMJ5%%-th part then his enjoyment of the Banh-mi will increase by xi%%ZSMJ6%% and the deliciousness of all the remaining parts will also increase by xi%%ZSMJ7%%. The initial enjoyment of JATC is equal to 0%%ZSMJ8%%.

For example, suppose the deliciousness of 3%%ZSMJ9%% parts are [0,1,0]%%ZSMJ10%%. If JATC eats the second part then his enjoyment will become 1%%ZSMJ11%% and the deliciousness of remaining parts will become [1,_,1]%%ZSMJ12%%. Next, if he eats the first part then his enjoyment will become 2%%ZSMJ13%% and the remaining parts will become [_,_,2]%%ZSMJ14%%. After eating the last part, JATC's enjoyment will become 4%%ZSMJ15%%.

However, JATC doesn't want to eat all the parts but to save some for later. He gives you q%%ZSMJ16%% queries, each of them consisting of two integers li%%ZSMJ17%% and ri%%ZSMJ18%%. For each query, you have to let him know what is the maximum enjoyment he can get if he eats all the parts with indices in the range [li,ri]%%ZSMJ19%% in some order.
All the queries are independent of each other. Since the answer to the query could be very large, print it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ20%%.
input: The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ21%% and q%%ZSMJ22%% (1≤n,q≤100000%%ZSMJ23%%).
The second line contains a string of n%%ZSMJ24%% characters, each character is either '0' or '1'. The i%%ZSMJ25%%-th character defines the deliciousness of the i%%ZSMJ26%%-th part.
Each of the following q%%ZSMJ27%% lines contains two integers li%%ZSMJ28%% and ri%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤li≤ri≤n%%ZSMJ30%%) — the segment of the corresponding query.
output: Print q%%ZSMJ31%% lines, where i%%ZSMJ32%%-th of them contains a single integer — the answer to the i%%ZSMJ33%%-th query modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ34%%.
note: For query 1%%ZSMJ35%%: One of the best ways for JATC to eats those parts is in this order: 1%%ZSMJ36%%, 4%%ZSMJ37%%, 3%%ZSMJ38%%, 2%%ZSMJ39%%.
For query 2%%ZSMJ40%%: Both 3%%ZSMJ41%%, 4%%ZSMJ42%% and 4%%ZSMJ43%%, 3%%ZSMJ44%% ordering give the same answer.
In the second example, any order of eating parts leads to the same answer.
